columns.comment: Payment message id (unique after the silver replay de-duplication).
columns.name: payment_id

columns.comment: Value / processing date of the payment.
columns.name: payment_date

columns.comment: First day of the month of payment_date.
columns.name: month

columns.comment: Surrogate key of the dim_client version valid on this row's date (SCD2 as-was join, D11); join to gold.dim_client.golden_client_sk for the client attributes at that time.
columns.name: golden_client_sk

columns.comment: Durable golden client id from entity resolution (GC-nnnnnn), stable across ER runs and SCD2 versions; one golden client = one resolved legal entity.
columns.name: golden_client_id

columns.comment: Client group (global parent group) id from the Tokyo HO group master (SYN-G-nnnn); join to gold.dim_client_group.
columns.name: client_group_id

columns.comment: Core-banking customer number (source identity record) of the paying / receiving client.
columns.name: cust_no

columns.comment: Client account debited (outbound) or credited (inbound); join gold.dim_account.
columns.name: account_id

columns.comment: APAC booking location of the client account (ISO-2); join gold.dim_booking_entity.
columns.name: booking_country

columns.comment: ISO 4217 currency of the client account the payment is booked to (the payments feed reports USD only).
columns.name: currency

columns.comment: Payment amount in USD (flow, always positive; direction gives the sign of the cash flow).
columns.name: amount_usd

columns.comment: Payment amount in the account currency, derived from amount_usd at the payment-date rate of gold.fx_rate_daily.
columns.name: amount_lcy

columns.comment: Inbound (client receives) or Outbound (client pays).
columns.name: direction

columns.comment: Channel / rail: SWIFT MT, ISO 20022, Host-to-Host, Payments API, Portal, RTGS or FAST.
columns.name: channel

columns.comment: Digital (Portal, Payments API, Host-to-Host - client-initiated electronically) or Network rail (SWIFT MT, ISO 20022, RTGS, FAST - where operations may still key manual instructions).
columns.name: channel_type

columns.comment: Supplier, Payroll, Tax, Intercompany, Loan Service, Dividend or Trade Settlement.
columns.name: payment_purpose

columns.comment: True when payment_purpose = Trade Settlement (trade flows visible from payments).
columns.name: is_trade_settlement

columns.comment: Country of the SMBC client side of the payment (the source's debtor_country field, which records the client's country for both directions).
columns.name: client_country

columns.comment: Country of the counterparty (beneficiary for outbound, remitter for inbound).
columns.name: counterparty_country

columns.comment: Country the money leaves: client_country for outbound, counterparty_country for inbound.
columns.name: payer_country

columns.comment: Country the money goes to: counterparty_country for outbound, client_country for inbound.
columns.name: payee_country

columns.comment: Money-flow corridor payer_country->payee_country, e.g. CN->VN (Kinokawa's China entity paying Vietnam).
columns.name: corridor

columns.comment: True for cross-border payments (as flagged by the payments hub).
columns.name: is_cross_border

columns.comment: SMBC (on-us), Other Bank (competitor bank) or Intercompany (transfer within the client group).
columns.name: counterparty_bank_type

columns.comment: Counterparty bank name (fictional competitors, SMBC or Intercompany).
columns.name: counterparty_bank_name

columns.comment: Counterparty bank key BNK-<NAME>; join gold.dim_competitor_bank.
columns.name: counterparty_bank_id

columns.comment: True when the counterparty banks with a competitor (Other Bank). Share paid via other banks = SUM(amount_usd WHERE true) / SUM(amount_usd) for outbound payments.
columns.name: is_other_bank_counterparty

columns.comment: Pseudonymous counterparty id for supplier and trade-settlement payments (count distinct = distinct suppliers / trading partners); null for other purposes.
columns.name: counterparty_ref

columns.comment: True when the payment went straight through (no manual repair). STP rate = count_if(stp_flag) / count(*).
columns.name: stp_flag

columns.comment: True when the payment needed a manual repair (not STP).
columns.name: is_repaired

columns.comment: Why the payment was repaired: FX cover missing, Invalid BIC, Missing beneficiary, Sanctions hold, Format error or Duplicate instruction; null for STP payments.
columns.name: repair_reason

columns.comment: End-to-end processing time in seconds (repairs take hours).
columns.name: processing_seconds

columns.comment: Payments product: PRD-CROSS-BORDER-PAYMENTS or PRD-DOMESTIC-PAYMENTS; join gold.dim_product.
columns.name: product_id

columns.comment: Payment fee income in USD from the bank's TB tariff used by the finance engine: USD 3 per payment message plus 10 bps of the value of cross-border payments (flow).
columns.name: fee_usd

comment: One row per client payment (inbound and outbound) through SMBC APAC from 1-Apr-2024 to 30-Sep-2026, after the silver de-duplication of the 17-Jun-2026 replay file (storyline 12: exactly one row per payment_id, totals equal silver): channel (SWIFT MT, ISO 20022, host-to-host, payments API, portal, RTGS, FAST), direction, purpose (supplier, payroll, tax, intercompany, loan service, dividend, trade settlement), client / counterparty / payer / payee country and money corridor, cross-border flag, counterparty bank (SMBC, a competitor bank or intercompany), STP / repair reason / processing time, the account currency and the tariff fee. Amounts are flows (additive). The richest signal source of the Customer 360: payments to other banks, supplier counts, trade corridors. Grain: one row per payment message (payment_id).
